name: OBGM (oral bacterial growth medium) + [U-13C]glycine (PMC3946380)
description: OBGM (oral bacterial growth medium) + [U-13C]glycine, medium reported in PMC3946380 (complex/undefined base, extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC3946380 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Full recipe recovered from the primary literature: base medium 'OBGM (oral bacterial growth medium)' (Full recipe published by the same group: Dashper SG et al. (2011) 'Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola Synergistic Polymicrobial Biofilm Development.' PLoS ONE 6(6):e27317, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0071727 (PMC3753311). Medium first named in Veith PD, Dashper SG, O'Brien-Simpson NM, et al. (2009) 'Major proteins and antigens of Treponema denticola.' Biochim Biophys Acta 1794:1421-14
provenance.verification_note: OBGM is a complex/undefined oral bacterial growth medium. This paper (PMC3946380) USES OBGM but does NOT reproduce its recipe (salts, carbon/N source, buffer, vitamins, trace elements, extracts); it cites external sources (Mitchell et al.; Veith et al.) for the formulation. Full component list therefore cannot be verified from this source and is left for manual review. VERIFIED CORRECTIONS vs curr
provenance.recipe_evidence: From PMC3946380: '[U-13C]glycine (Cambridge Isotope Laboratories, MA, USA) was added to a final concentration of 5 mM' to cultures grown 'in oral bacterial growth medium (OBGM), that meets the growth requirements of both P. gingivalis and T. denticola', maintained anaerobically at 37C (5% CO2, 5% H2, 90% N2 batch; 10% CO2 in N2 continuous). Full OBGM recipe from the same group (PMC3753311 / PLoS ONE, Dashper et al. 2011): 'OBGM contained brain heart infusion (12.5 g/L), tryptone soya broth (10 g/L), yeast extract (7.5 g/L), sodium thioglycolate (0.5 g/L), asparagine (0.25 g/L) D-glucose (2 g/L
provenance.base_medium_reference: Full recipe published by the same group: Dashper SG et al. (2011) 'Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola Synergistic Polymicrobial Biofilm Development.' PLoS ONE 6(6):e27317, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0071727 (PMC3753311). Medium first named in Veith PD, Dashper SG, O'Brien-Simpson NM, et al. (2009) 'Major proteins and antigens of Treponema denticola.' Biochim Biophys Acta 1794:1421-1432, doi:10.1016/j.bbapap.2009.06.001 (ref [27] in PMC3946380), but that paper does not tabulate the full composition.

yeast extract.citation: Yeast extract = autolysate of Saccharomyces cerevisiae: free amino acids (glutamate/alanine/aspartate-rich, essential AAs ~40% of total), B-vitamins (B1 thiamine, B2 riboflavin, B3 niacin, B5 pantothenate, B6 pyridoxine, B7 biotin, B9 folate, B12), RNA-derived 5'-nucleotides/nucleosides (~10-15%), and minerals (K, P, Mg, Zn, Mn). Quantitative composition: Tao Z et al., J Microbiol Biotechnol 2022;32:1236-1247, doi:10.4014/jmb.2207.07057 (PMC9998214); Podpora B et al., Czech J Food Sci 2016;34:554-563, doi:10.17221/419/2015-CJFS; Atlas RM, Handbook of Microbiological Media, doi:10.1201/EBK1439804063.

tryptone soya broth.citation: Tryptone = pancreatic (tryptic) digest of casein; amino-acid-rich, tryptophan retained. Source: BD Bionutrient Technical Manual; casein amino-acid profile (FAO/WHO).

provenance.verification_downgrade_reason: Downgraded from 'paper-verified (recipe recovered from primary literature)': the project's verification pass recorded verdict 'unavailable' (tools/verification_verdicts.tsv); and the record's own provenance.verification_note contradicts the label. The cited work does not contain this formulation; the recipe was reconstructed from references chased out of it.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
